The visual evoked potential results showing prolonged latency and reduced amplitude strongly suggest demyelination or optic nerve dysfunction. Given the subacute 3-week progression of headache, bilateral visual changes, and these specific test findings, I need to confirm if you have any recent upper respiratory infection or if the pain is located at the base of your skull.

REQUEST TEST: Lumbar_Puncture. Please report if you experience any sensitivity to light or a headache that worsens significantly when you sit up or stand.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: Lumbar_Puncture: Cerebrospinal fluid analysis shows increased opening pressure, elevated white blood cell count with lymphocytic predominance, and elevated protein levels. The patient reports significant headache that worsens when sitting up or standing and notes photophobia. No blood xanthochromia detected. These findings are consistent with aseptic meningitis or inflammatory optic neuropathy.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Idiopathic Intracranial Hypertension (Pseudotumor Cerebri) with secondary Optic Neuropathy.

The combination of elevated opening pressure, lymphocytic pleocytosis, and headache that worsens when upright is highly suggestive of IIH, likely exacerbated by the inflammatory response of the optic nerve. I request the MRI images specifically to look for the classic "empty sella" sign and confirm the absence of a mass lesion.
